newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: REED SEES U.S. TRADE PRESS MARGINS REACHING 20 PCT.
newsitem.headline: REED SEES U.S. TRADE PRESS MARGINS REACHING 20 PCT.

text.p: Anglo-Dutch publisher Reed-Elsevier said on Monday it believed it could raise its margins in U.S. business-to-business publishing to some 20 percent in two years from 15 to 17 percent now.

Group strategy director Peter van Hooff told Reuters that by bringing together the newly acquired Chilton Business Group with its Cahners Publishing Co unit, Reed Elsevier could squeeze extra revenues and cost-savings out of the combined group.
"Chilton's operating margins are around 15 percent... but we strongly believe that with the combination of the two we can increase it by about one third to 20 percent," he said.
Van Hooff said Cahners had an operating margin of 16 to 17 percent but this too would rise to around 20 percent by 1999.
Reed Elsevier, announcing its second major U.S. acquisition this year, said on Monday it would buy Chilton from Walt Disney Co subsidiary ABC for $447 million in cash.
Van Hooff said the deal would significantly strengthen Reed Elsevier's U.S. trade magazine publishing business, providing plenty of scope to raise revenues and cut costs.
"The combination of Cahners and Chilton gives us even stronger positions in more markets," he said.
Van Hooff said Reed Elsevier would reap benefits by eliminating overlap between previously competing titles and making them more complementary.
Avertising sales forces could be merged and combined rate cards could be offered to advertisers.
The Chilton acquisition will also substantially reduce Reed Elsevier's U.S. tax bill by allowing it to offset amortisation of intangible assets against taxes.
"We can amortise some 80 or 90 percent of the purchase price over 15 years at a tax rate of 40 percent," Van Hooff said.
Van Hooff said the Chilton titles would broaden and deepen the editorial content which Reed Elsevier was able to offer via electronic publishing platforms.
The Chilton titles, which did not previously have their own electronic outlet, would draw immediate benefits from their access to Reed Elsevier's electronic distribution.
"The Chilton titles will really benefit from the lead we have in electronic publishing," Van Hooff said.

Van Hooff said Reed Elsevier, which publishes the U.S. showbusiness newspaper Variety, said the group had already been working on plans to develop an online news and information service for the entertainment industry.
Chilton's entertainment titles would add further momentum to this project, he said. -- Andrew Kelly, Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000
